run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T13:26:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is explained by a loss of the ad serving backend during a rollout of the ad Deployment. At 2026-11-16T13:25:14Z the ad Deployment's pod template was annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:25:14Z (generation 2), a new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 was created, and the old (and only) pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq was deleted at 13:25:17. The ad pod template defines no readiness probe, so the replacement pod was added to the ad Service endpoints as soon as its container started (13:25:16), although the application only logged 'Ad service starting.' at 13:29:27 and produced no oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans from about 13:26 until roughly 13:34. In exactly that interval frontend produced STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans only on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, tcp.connect, GET and the /api/data route (its other routes had none), and frontend-proxy reported ingress/egress error spans; all of these returned to zero from ~13:35, when ad began serving again. The frontend pods themselves were Running/Ready with zero restarts, and ad's own spans carried no error status: ad was unreachable, not returning errors. Additional supporting factor: the new ad container was heavily CPU-throttled (5622.6 throttled CFS periods per 300s ending 13:30 versus ~296 for the old pod) while consuming 0.083-0.099 cores against a 50m CPU limit, consistent with its ~4-minute delay before starting to serve.

claims.text: At 13:26:25Z frontend had STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate 0.5 spans/s alongside STATUS_CODE_UNSET 44.57 spans/s, whereas increase() over the preceding hour was 0 for STATUS_CODE_ERROR up to the bucket ending 13:21:25Z.

Frontend error spans were confined to specific operations: in the 600s bucket ending 13:26:25Z only span_name GET (33.68), GET /api/data (33.68), executing api route (pages) /api/data (33.68), grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (33.68) and tcp.connect (7.37) were non-zero; GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder were 0.

The frontend error burst started between 13:25 and 13:26 (0 at 13:24:00 and 13:25:00 points, 270 in the 60s bucket ending 13:26:00, peaking at 468), stayed elevated through 13:33, and was 0 from 13:34/13:35 onward.

ad produced no oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans during the frontend error interval: the 120s increase() was 0 at every point from 13:28:00 through 13:34:00, then 80.95 at 13:35:00, 96.05, 137.33, 146.67 and 128.59; the 300s view shows GetAds 285.56 (bucket ending 13:25:00) dropping to 36.25 (13:30:00), 80.95 (13:35:00) and recovering to 204.19 (13:40:00).

ad's own spans reported no error status: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory, getRandomAds and resolve were all STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR series under service_name=ad was flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at ~1.11 per 300s, which also appears for fraud-detection and recommendation.

The ad Deployment was rolled at 13:25:14Z: pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was Scheduled 13:25:14Z, container Created/Started 13:25:15-16Z, while pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq was deleted (SuccessfulDelete) and its container stopped (Killing) at 13:25:17Z; the new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 has 1 ready replica and the old ad-554b849958 now has 0.

Deployment ad is at generation 2 / observedGeneration 2 with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt="2026-11-16T13:25:14Z"; its container image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), env, ports and resources are identical between the old ad-554b849958 and new ad-d89765fb5 pod templates, so the rollout was a manual restart rather than a visible configuration change.

The ad pod template has no readinessProbe (null in both ReplicaSets), the Deployment has 1 replica, RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable 25% / maxSurge 25% and no minReadySeconds; Service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad on port 8080->8080 and its Endpoints at query time contained ad-d89765fb5-whfnz:8080.

The new ad container logged only "Ad service starting." at 2026-11-16T13:29:27.903167Z, about four minutes after its container was Started at 13:25:16Z and about five minutes after the old pod was removed.

The new ad container ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was heavily CPU-throttled: increase of container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total was 5622.65 per 300s ending 13:30:00 and 3364.77 ending 13:35:00, falling to 271.95 ending 13:40:00, versus 295.55 and 197.67 for the old pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq; CPU usage was 0.083-0.099 cores at 13:27-13:32 versus 0.009-0.014 for the old pod, against a 50m CPU limit / 10m request.

frontend-proxy reported its own error spans in the same interval: ingress 257.5 (300s bucket ending 13:30:00) and 196.67 (ending 13:35:00), with router frontend egress 257.5 and 176.67 in the same buckets and 0 in the buckets before and after.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready at query time; frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 was Ready with 0 restarts and started at 12:52:47Z, and ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was Ready with 0 restarts, so neither frontend nor the replacement ad container crashed or restarted during the event.

Service-level error comparison over the 1200s ending 13:26:25Z shows frontend as the dominant error source (138.46 error spans) with frontend-proxy 75.9 and only trace-level noise for ad (1.02), fraud-detection (1.02) and recommendation (2.05).

No Warning-type events existed in namespace otel-demo inside the authorized window; the only ad-related events were the Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing/SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate records of the 13:25:14-13:25:17 rollout.

The alert fired because the manual restartedAt rollout of Deployment ad removed the only serving ad replica before the replacement JVM was listening on port 8080; with no readiness probe the new pod was routed immediately, so frontend's GetAds calls could not connect (its tcp.connect and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error spans) and its /api/data route returned errors, which frontend-proxy surfaced as ingress errors. The causal order is supported by the coincident start (rollout 13:25:14, first frontend error bucket 13:26:00), the matching span set, ad's silent span gap, and the joint recovery at ~13:34-13:35.

The ad replacement's slow availability (~4 minutes to log 'Ad service starting.' and roughly 8-9 minutes before GetAds traffic resumed) was prolonged by CPU starvation: the container hit its 50m CPU limit while burning 0.083-0.099 cores and accumulating thousands of throttled CFS periods per 5 minutes, whereas the old container ran at ~0.01 cores with ~200-300 throttled periods.

The fraud-detection OOMKill was not the cause of this alert: its container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 12:58:09Z, about 27 minutes before the frontend error onset at 13:25-13:26, and its only error spans are the same ~1 per 5 min flagd EventStream noise seen in ad and recommendation.

The flagd rollout was not the cause: Deployment flagd carries restartedAt=2026-11-16T12:54:23Z and its pod started at 12:54:23Z, roughly 30 minutes before the frontend error onset, and frontend error spans were 0 in every bucket from 12:26 to 13:25.

ad was not crashed or mislabelled: the ad Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad matched the new pod in Endpoints on port 8080, the ad container had 0 restarts with no terminating last state, and ad's own GetAds spans never carried an error status - so the fault is a startup/availability gap, not an application error or a service-selector mismatch.

Add a readinessProbe to the ad container (gRPC/TCP on port 8080, with adequate initialDelaySeconds/failureThreshold for JVM start) and, for a 1-replica Deployment, avoid restarting it during traffic or raise replicas so maxUnavailable 25% cannot take the sole serving replica out; also consider raising the ad CPU limit/request above 50m/10m so JVM startup is not throttled for minutes.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so who or what triggered the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:25:14Z patch on Deployment ad, and whether a competing reason existed, could not be verified.

Jaeger's sampled traces did not cover the error period: the frontend trace sample held spans only from 13:22:57-13:22:59, and tag searches for error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR" and otel.status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" and operation-filtered GetAds searches in 13:25-13:35 returned no traces, so no gRPC status code or connection-error message from the failing GetAds/tcp.connect spans could be read.
The frontend container produced no log lines in 13:20-13:40 that the log API could return, so the application-side error text for the 13:25-13:34 /api/data failures is unverified.

Deployment-level readiness series kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no data in the window, so ad's ready-replica count during the outage could not be read from Prometheus and was taken from the pod/ReplicaSet objects and events instead.

No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate exists in this Prometheus, so the alert expression, its window and the exact meaning of the reported value 2.355555555555555 could not be verified against the alert annotation.

Whether the ad pod was considered Ready (and therefore an endpoint) for the whole 13:25:16-13:29:27 interval is inferred from the absent readiness probe and the present Endpoints entry at query time; the cluster objects expose only the current state, not the state during that interval.
next_steps: Confirm with the cluster change log/CI who issued the restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-16T13:25:14Z and why.
Add a readiness probe (and where applicable a startup probe) to the ad container and review the 50m CPU limit for the ad JVM so restart-induced unavailability cannot recur.
Consider running ad with more than one replica, or setting a PodDisruptionBudget/maxUnavailable of 0 for single-replica services in otel-demo.
If trace-level error text is needed, increase Jaeger retention/sampling coverage or query the otel-collector logs for the 13:25-13:35 gRPC failures.
Separately review the fraud-detection container's 400Mi memory limit, which produced an OOMKill (exit 137) at 12:58:09Z unrelated to this alert.
